name: Vector Representation
description: Learn about Vector Representation and its applications in physics.

content.overview: So you've got a vector - now how do you actually write it down or draw it? Turns out there's more than one way, and they're all just different ways of saying the same thing. {{viz:diagram-01}}
keyPoints: A vector can be drawn as an arrow, written as components (vx, vy), or given as magnitude + angle {{viz:diagram-02}}
Components add straight across: add the x's together, add the y's together {{viz:chart-01}}
All three forms describe the exact same vector - just pick whichever is easiest for the problem
content.whyItMatters: Nearly every physics problem with forces or motion asks you to switch between these representations - breaking a force into components, or turning components back into a magnitude and direction. Get comfortable with all three and vector problems stop feeling like a foreign language.
